review_notes: I read the whole file. I looked for repeated nontrivial arguments and found little in the Hilbert/tabloid part. The two fiber-cardinality lemmas (card_row_fiber/card_col_fiber) and card_rowGroup/card_colGroup are near-duplicates, but each is 3–4 lines of routine unfolding, so I did not report them. The Specht/FiniteCharacters part has no real duplication. The one repeated block is the `ht` hypothesis (transitivity plus invariance of hilbertSpace under permutations of tabloids), which is rebuilt inline in two theorems. It is only about four lines, so the benefit is modest. I could not run Lean, so the proposed lemma has not been compiled. I expect the rewrite to typecheck, since the proof body is copied verbatim and both uses supply exactly the `htrans` argument.

findings.excerpt: have ht (f g : Tabloid μ) : ∃ p : Equiv.Perm (Tabloid μ), p f = g ∧
findings.problem: Both theorems build the same hypothesis `htrans` for the PermutationHilbert API inline. The hypothesis says the permutation action on tabloids is transitive and that each permutation preserves hilbertSpace μ. The 4-line proof is the same in both: get p from tabloidAct_transitive, then use tabloidAct p together with hilbertSpace_invariant. Only spacing differs (`p f = g` vs `p f=g`). The fact is a standalone property of hilbertSpace μ, so each caller restating the proof obscures what it is.
findings.proposed_change:
Add, right after `hilbertSpace_invariant` and `tabloidAct_transitive` (around line 385), a lemma:

lemma hilbertSpace_transitive (μ : YoungDiagram) (f g : Tabloid μ) :
    ∃ p : Equiv.Perm (Tabloid μ), p f = g ∧
      (hilbertSpace μ).map (PermutationHilbert.act p).toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap = hilbertSpace μ := by
  obtain ⟨p,hp⟩ := tabloidAct_transitive μ f g
  exact ⟨tabloidAct p,hp,hilbertSpace_invariant μ p⟩

Then delete both inline `have ht` blocks. In dimension_times_column_ge_tabloids use `PermutationHilbert.uncertainty (hilbertSpace μ) (hilbertSpace_transitive μ) (hilbertEquiv μ (polytabloid μ)) ⟨polytabloid μ,polytabloid_mem_space μ,rfl⟩ (baseTabloid μ)`. In fixedHilbert_dimension use `PermutationHilbert.footprint_dimension (hilbertSpace μ) (fixedHilbert μ A) (fixedHilbert_le μ A) (hilbertSpace_transitive μ) (footprint μ A) hproj`. Both calls pass exactly the `htrans : ∀ x y, ∃ p, p x = y ∧ W.map ... = W` argument they pass today, so the hypotheses and imports are unchanged. The rewritten uses should still typecheck.
findings.benefit: The transitivity-plus-invariance fact is stated and proved once and has a name. Each theorem then shows only its own argument, and any change to the PermutationHilbert interface (for example the form of `htrans`) needs one edit instead of two parallel ones.
